title: Sawa Marian
name: Sawa Marian
description: composer, organist, and educator; b. January 12, 1937, in Krasnystaw; d. April 27, 2005, in Warsaw. He studied organ under Feliks Rączkowski (graduating in 1963) and composition under Kazimierz Sikorski (graduating in 1968) at the State Higher School of Music in Warsaw. While still a student, he served as an organist at the Garrison Church in Warsaw (1956–66). From 1966, he worked at the Józef Elsner Secondary Music School in Warsaw; from 1973, at the Academy of Music in Warsaw; from 1992 to 2003, at the Department of Church Musicology of the Cardinal Stefan Wyszyński University; and from 2002, at the State Music School No. 4 in Warsaw. As an organist, he collaborated with numerous ensembles and artists, including Jerzy Artysz, Jadwiga Gadulanka, Pola Lipińska, Bernard Ładysz, Anna Malewicz-Madey, Leonard Andrzej Mróz, Wiesław Ochman, Jerzy Połomski, Sława Przybylska, Kazimierz Pustelak, Ryszarda Racewicz, Jadwiga Rappé, Paulos Raptis, Irena Santor, and Krystyna Szostek-Rad rs. He formed an organ duet with Marietta Kruzel-Sosnowska, performing his own works composed for two organists. He recorded organ pieces for various record labels—including Polskie Nagrania, DUX, Veriton, Polskie Nagrania Edition, Polonia Records, MTJ, and Acte Préalable—as well as for Polish Radio and Polish Television. He performed in Poland and abroad, including in Belgium, Finland, France, the Netherlands, Germany, Italy, and the countries of the former Soviet Union. Marian Sawa’s exceptionally rich number of works comprises primarily organ and choral pieces. His compositions have been showcased during numerous recitals and festivals, including the "Gaude Mater" International Festival of Sacred Music in Częstochowa, the Laboratory of Contemporary Music in Białystok, the "Wratislavia Cantans" Festival, the Organ Conversatorium in Legnica, the Musica Sacra International Festival in Łódź, the Rev. Stanisław Ormiński International Festival of Religious Music in Rumia, the Warsaw Music Encounters, as well as organ music festivals in Frombork, Gniezno, Kamień Pomorski, Kazimierz Dolny, Koszalin, Koronowo, Kraków, Legnica, Leżajsk, Lublin, Łódź, Morąg, Oliwa, Olsztyn, Pelplin, Radom, Rumia, Poznań, Sejny, Szczecin, Warsaw, and Władysławowo, as well as abroad (including Belgium, Finland, France, the Netherlands, Germany, Russia, Italy, and the United States). A special organ festival entirely dedicated to his music was established in Sejny. He was a member of the Society of Authors ZAiKS and the Musica Sacra Association. He served multiple times as a juror for organ, choral, and composition competitions. Marian Sawa received numerous awards and distinctions for his compositional work, including the 1st prize at the Polish Composers' Union Youth Competition in 1969 for the piece Assemblage for orchestra (1969), and the 3rd prize at the Composition Competition announced by the Main Board of the Polish Association of Choirs and Orchestras in 1987 for Dyptyk wiejski ( Rural Diptych ) for mixed a cappella choir. He was also a recipient of recording awards: in 2000, he won 1st prize at the 15th International Film and Multimedia Festival in Niepokalanów for the album Marian Sawa – Organ Music I , and in 2001, the album Marian Sawa – Organ Music II was nominated for the "Fryderyk 2001" award. Furthermore, he was honored with the Award of the Minister of Education for outstanding achievements in educational work (1975), the Award of the Minister of Culture and Art, 2nd Class (1979), and the Gold Cross of Merit (1985). In 2006, on the 1st anniversary of the composer's death, the Marian Sawa Society was established in Warsaw. updated: May 2006 Website dedicated to the composer: www.mariansawa.org
